ECON-MG-ELITE-318.reason: Distinguish the seller incidence rectangle from total PS loss and revenue.

ECON-MG-LEGENDARY-9071.q: Supply is perfectly inelastic at 200 units and demand slopes downward. A $6 tax is imposed in a competitive market with no externalities or collection costs. Which combination follows?
options: Sellers bear $6 per unit, revenue is $1,200, and deadweight loss is zero
Buyers bear $6 per unit, revenue is $1,200, and deadweight loss is zero
Sellers bear $6 per unit, revenue is $1,200, and deadweight loss is $1,200
Buyers and sellers each bear $3, revenue is $600, and quantity falls
ECON-MG-LEGENDARY-9071.feedback: The vertical supply curve holds quantity at 200. Buyers pay the same demand price at that quantity, so sellers absorb the full $6 wedge through lower net receipts. Revenue is $1,200. With no trades lost and no other distortions in the stated model, tax revenue is a transfer and there is no deadweight loss.
ECON-MG-LEGENDARY-9071.reason: Connect an extreme incidence case to quantity, revenue and welfare instead of repeating the burden rule.
